brief: A captured authentication hash belongs to an ANUS INDUSTRIES HR account. Read the dossier, collect password fragments, and crack the hash on your rented compute relay. Keep Exposure below 100.

facts.label: His favourite person isn't a person
facts.note: “All my important accounts are named after Barsik. People betray you. A cat at least makes eye contact.” His previous cat was called Fluffy.

facts.label: Employee record
facts.note: Alex uses his full birth year in memorable numbers. Reason for employment: “Not dead yet.”

facts.label: Public handle
facts.note: Human Remains Manager. “We are not a family. You can't downsize your family every quarter.”

facts.label: An old password
facts.note: No longer valid. Notice the pattern: capitalized name, four-digit year, exclamation mark. Fluffy has since been promoted to cloud storage.

facts.label: A message to IT
facts.value: “Now I replace lowercase a with @. Name first, year next, ! at the end. Secure enough?”
facts.note: Posted after his last password change. IT replied: “That's my thirteenth reason to quit.”

solution.explanation: His current cat is Barsik. Add his birth year, 1990, and follow the old password's capital letter and !. The message to IT explains a → @. You cracked a habit, not a cipher.
